posts.title: Xiaomi's EV and AI business posts second straight quarterly loss
posts.summary:
Xiaomi's new initiatives, which include EV and AI, posted a loss from operations of 2.6 billion yuan ($383 million) in the second quarter.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi's EV and AI segment reported a 2.6 billion yuan operating loss in Q2 2026, marking the second consecutive quarterly loss despite a 17.1% year-on-year revenue increase.
Gross margins for the segment contracted to 19.2% from 26.4% a year earlier, driven by higher component costs and increased investment in AI infrastructure.
While the segment remains in the red, Xiaomi continues to see strong demand, delivering 104,199 vehicles in the second quarter, bringing cumulative SU7 series deliveries past 500,000 units.

posts.title: BYD Fang Cheng Bao to debut Tai 9 SUV at Chengdu Auto Show
posts.summary:
The 6-seat plug-in hybrid SUV measures 5,270 mm in length, making it Fang Cheng Bao's largest model.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD's Fang Cheng Bao brand will debut the Tai 9, a 6-seat plug-in hybrid SUV, at the upcoming Chengdu Auto Show, marking the brand's largest model to date at 5,270 mm in length.
The Tai 9 is built on BYD's new DMS platform and features a 1.5-liter engine paired with dual electric motors, offering a battery-only range of 310 kilometers.
Fang Cheng Bao continues to scale rapidly, reporting a 190.6% year-on-year sales increase in July and surpassing 500,000 cumulative units sold in under three years.

posts.title: AI’s recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all
posts.summary: The AI industry’s boldest promise right now is that AI will soon improve itself, with almost no need for human oversight. LLMs can already write code, generate synthetic data for training, and optimize the computer chips they run on. Forecasts of explosive AI progress predict that what researchers call recursive self-improvement is on the horizon. …
bullets: New research from Princeton suggests that current AI agents lack the judgment and creativity required for open-ended, innovative research, challenging the timeline for recursive self-improvement.
While AI models excel at narrow engineering tasks, they struggle with high-level research activities like hypothesis generation and determining when to abandon unproductive lines of inquiry.
The study utilized a 'shadow evaluation' method, testing models like Claude Opus 4.8 against unpublished NeurIPS 2026 papers to measure their ability to perform original scientific work.

The findings indicate that the industry's hype regarding fully automated, self-improving AI research may be premature, as models currently fail to meet the standards of top-tier machine learning conferences.

posts.title: Semiconductor Earnings Roundup: Revenue, Growth and Takeaways
posts.summary:
Company-by-company breakdown: Earnings across 80 semiconductor companies show AI-driven demand extending well beyond the usual suspects.
The post Semiconductor Earnings Roundup: Revenue, Growth and Takeaways appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Company-by-company breakdown: Earnings across 80 semiconductor companies show AI-driven demand extending well beyond the usual suspects.
Note: Updated throughout August 2026 for additional earnings releases.
Earnings were strong across all chip industry sectors this quarter, with 11 companies posting triple-digit growth, and all but 2 of the 80 companies reported here were in positive territory.
The hottest growth areas were AI infrastructure, memory, advanced packaging, test and leading-edge manufacturing.
Companies tied to HBM, data centers and AI accelerators generally posted the strongest growth, while handset and consumer-related results were more mixed.
